belief: It's in my genes, so there's no point trying.
origins: When a condition has a genetic component, some conclude that effort, treatment, and habits are pointless. This fatalism can keep people from the very steps that help.
teaches: “Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.” “Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.” God invites us to be wise stewards of the bodies and minds He gave. Genes load the dice but do not decide every roll. Diet, sleep, exercise, therapy, medication, and relationships often change outcomes significantly. “I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength” (Philippians 4:13).
self_statements: Nothing I do will make a difference.
I may as well give up.
errors: Believing outcomes are either all genes or all effort.
Feeling helpless and concluding that effort is useless.
Calling myself a victim of my genes.
questions: What does my doctor say about what can be done?
What lifestyle or treatment steps help even with a genetic risk?
Do I know people who managed well despite genetics?
What would trying look like in a small way?
What does Scripture say about not giving up?
Who can help me stay motivated?
truth: Genes are one factor, not the whole story. Wise effort, good care, and God’s help matter. I can take small steps and not give up.
hw_truths: I can do all things through Christ.
log: Each week, note one helpful step you took.
actions: Learn what helps for your condition.
prayer: Lord, I feel that nothing matters. Give me wisdom to do what I can, strength to keep going, and trust that You work in my effort. Amen.
